First listed 2025-10-22 · episode or wrap

Inside the Data Center Boom: Understanding the Massive Infrastructure That Supports AI

Nick Del Deo explains the distinct economics of data-center property, interconnection hubs, GPU clouds and fiber. The strongest framework separates recurring cash metrics from expansion capex and models CoreWeave contract-level lifetime returns rather than applying peer EBITDA multiples. He expects eventual competition and power supply to reduce scarcity returns but avoids a precise collapse date. Later Equinix growth was stronger than the reported early 2026 plan, while Lumen's legacy decline remained visible.

Right
Source · 11:40-17:09 ↗

Materialitymajor

The conditional relationship follows from the explicit assumptions; it does not establish that those assumptions hold in observed markets.

Qualification: Conditional mechanism, not an independently measured moat size or proof of every historical profit estimate.

Conditional reasoning

Adding relevant counterparties raises connection opportunities and customer value. A building alone lacks those links, so duplicating physical space does not instantly duplicate the network benefit.

  • Customers value direct links to counterparties colocated in a facility.
  • A new competitor initially lacks that established counterpart network.

Right
Source · 20:24-21:54 ↗
SpeakerNick Del Deo
Stanceasserted
Horizonnot stated
Materialitymajor

The conditional relationship follows from the explicit assumptions; it does not establish that those assumptions hold in observed markets.

Conditional reasoning

A small extra delay to a user endpoint is negligible relative to the long training run, whereas slow internal links repeated throughout computation can constrain performance. This distinguishes external location latency from internal cluster latency.

  • A training run lasts weeks or months and does not require real-time responses to a distant user.
  • Its distributed compute still requires fast internal communication.

How he reasons here

  • Map property ownership, equipment ownership and customer obligations separately.
  • Distinguish network effects from temporary physical scarcity.
  • Value GPU projects over equipment life, including capex, financing, renewals and residual value.
  • Lifetime NPV per invested dollar is not an annual return on capital.
  • Check final user latency separately from latency inside a training cluster.
  • Deduplicate utility requests and distinguish planned, contracted and energized power.
